# InnovateUS: full text

> InnovateUS (innovate-us.org) provides no-cost, at-your-own-pace and live learning on data, digital, innovation and AI skills for public service professionals. It is a partner project of the Burnes Center for Social Change, The GovLab, Reboot Democracy and AI for Impact.

This file holds every public workshop (40 upcoming, 355 past) with its description, learning goals, speakers and recording, and every news post (52) in full. Each entry starts with a header between --- lines (id, title, url, date, people) and is also available on its own at its page's address plus .md; for a recorded workshop that copy also holds the transcript of the recording. When you use this material, cite and link the page on innovate-us.org, not this file. The list of all pages with short teasers is https://innovate-us.org/llms.txt.

## At-your-own-pace courses

- [AI For Public Sector Procurement](https://innovate-us.org/course/ai-for-public-sector-procurement): Developed in collaboration with Partners for Public Good with support from the National Association for State Procurement Officials, this course will equip procurement and other public sector professionals with the skills to use Generative AI to improve competitiveness, effectiveness and efficiency…
- [Designing Democratic Engagement with AI](https://innovate-us.org/course/democratic-engagement-for-ai-era): This free, self-paced course equips you with the skills to design, run and learn from meaningful engagement with communities.
- [Driving Innovation in Government: From Ideas to Scaled Impact](https://innovate-us.org/course/driving-innovation-in-government): In this course, Professor Anita McGahan equips public professionals with practical strategies to design, test, and scale innovations—leveraging AI and new technologies and private sector collaboration to improve the public good.
- [Human-Centered Design](https://innovate-us.org/course/human-centered-design): Designed by Virginia Hamilton, this course gives participants a substantive overview of the human-centered design framework and offers opportunities to practice applying concepts from the course to your work.
- [Open Justice](https://innovate-us.org/course/open-justice): Open justice is a growing movement to use new technologies, including big data, digital platforms, blockchain and more, to improve our legal system by making the workings of our legal institutions easier to understand, scrutinize and, we hope, improve.
- [Responsible AI for Public Organizations](https://innovate-us.org/course/responsible-ai-for-public-organizations): This two-part course guides public sector professionals through building impactful, responsible AI initiatives. Learn to align AI with agency goals, manage risks, and develop necessary skills. Free, self-paced, and open to all interested in using AI to transform government work.
- [Responsible AI for Public Professionals](https://innovate-us.org/course/responsible-ai-for-public-professionals): Through hands-on activities, these free courses showcase the practical ways you can use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in your work as a public professional. Addresses what to do and how to avoid risks.
- [Responsible AI for Public Sector Legal Professionals](https://innovate-us.org/course/responsible-ai-for-public-sector-legal-professionals): This two-part course is designed for public sector legal professionals at all levels who are interested in learning more about safe and responsible individual use of GenAI tools.
- [The Innovation Skills Accelerator.](https://innovate-us.org/course/innovation-skills-accelerator): Based on research with thousands of public servants across three continents, our problem-solving curriculum gives you the digital, data and innovation skills to deliver more effective, equitable and engaged policies and services.
- [What Works: Fast Field Scanning with AI](https://innovate-us.org/course/what-works-fast-field-scanning-with-ai): This course is designed to help public professionals accelerate the process of finding and implementing urgently-needed evidence-based solutions to public problems. This course is brought to you in partnership with Results for America and Solutions Journalism Network.

# From Prompts to Workflows

InnovateUS workshop · 30 November 2026 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Most public professionals use AI one task at a time. Agents offer the possibility of creating reusable workflows that can support recurring work. This session explores how agencies are using agentic workflows for research, communications, permitting, grants management, procurement, case preparation, constituent services, and other operational activities. Participants will learn how to identify workflows that may benefit from agentic approaches and where simpler tools may be sufficient.

## Speakers

- **William (Bill) Resh**, Chair & Professor of Public Management & Policy; Director, Civic Leadership Education & Research Initiative; Co-Chair, Accountability & Reform Research Consortium (Volcker Alliance)

## Moderators

- **Deborah Stine**, Senior Fellow, Innovate US

# The Rise of the Citizen Developer

InnovateUS workshop · 1 December 2026 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

AI is expanding who can help build and improve government services. Policy experts, analysts, program managers, and frontline staff can now use AI-enabled tools to prototype applications, automate routine workflows, and solve operational problems that once required specialized technical support.

In this workshop, you will explore how public agencies can support citizen developers while maintaining the governance, training, and oversight needed to innovate responsibly. You will learn how AI fellowships, internal support models, and cross-functional collaboration can help agencies turn staff expertise into practical service improvements.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Identify **opportunities for nontechnical staff to use AI-enabled tools to improve workflows and services.
- **Apply **governance and support practices that help citizen developers innovate responsibly.
- **Evaluate **training, fellowship, and collaboration models that build internal AI capacity.

## Speakers

- **Sofía Bosch Gómez**, Assistant Professor in the Department of Art + Design and Fellow at the Burnes Center for Social Change, Northeastern University

## Moderators

- **Anirudh Dinesh**, CTO, InnovateUS

Part of the series [AI Insourcing and the Government Product Model](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/ai-insourcing-and-the-government-product-model-).

# When AI Creates New Risks

InnovateUS workshop · 2 December 2026 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

AI introduces new ways for information to be exposed, manipulated, or misused, while AI systems themselves can create new security and operational vulnerabilities. Using real-world examples, this session examines how AI is changing the security landscape for government, including risks related to data leakage, prompt injection, public-facing AI tools, shadow AI, and other emerging threats. Participants will learn to recognize how seemingly routine uses of AI can create significant security and operational consequences—and what to watch for in their own work.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Identify** common cybersecurity and operational risks associated with the use of AI in government.
- **Recognize** how risks such as data leakage, prompt injection, and shadow AI can emerge in everyday work.
- **Assess** how routine decisions about using AI tools can create broader risks for their teams and organizations.

## Speakers

- **Nicol Turner Lee**, Senior Fellow and Director, Center for Technology Innovation Brookings Institution

## Moderators

- **Deborah Stine**, Senior Fellow, Innovate US

Part of the series [AI and Cybersecurity in the Public Sector for the Non-Expert](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/ai-and-cybersecurity-in-the-public-sector-for-the-non-expert).

Register on the workshop page: https://innovate-us.org/when-ai-creates-new-risks

# Building High-Performing Product Teams

InnovateUS workshop · 3 December 2026 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

AI-enabled services are not built by technology teams alone. Strong public-sector products require collaboration across product, design, engineering, procurement, policy, legal, program, and service delivery teams — each bringing knowledge that helps ensure the product is useful, responsible, and sustainable.

In this workshop, you will explore how high-performing product teams work in government. You will learn how different roles can collaborate across the product lifecycle, from defining the problem and setting priorities to managing risks, governing AI use, and improving services over time.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Identify **the roles and skills needed to build and manage AI-enabled public-sector products.
- **Apply **collaboration practices that help product, technical, policy, legal, and program teams work together effectively.
- **Evaluate **governance and operating models that support responsible product development over time.

## Moderators

- **Anirudh Dinesh**, CTO, InnovateUS

Part of the series [AI Insourcing and the Government Product Model](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/ai-insourcing-and-the-government-product-model-).

# Bringing Agents to Work

InnovateUS workshop · 7 December 2026 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Technology adoption is ultimately a people challenge. How do agencies help staff move from occasional AI use to meaningful integration into everyday work? This session examines strategies for workforce adoption, training, change management, experimentation, and learning. Participants will explore how organizations are helping employees identify high-value use cases, redesign workflows, build confidence in agentic tools, and create feedback loops that improve both performance and governance over time.

# Evaluating AI Tools and Vendors

InnovateUS workshop · 9 December 2026 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

This session examines the questions public officials should ask before adopting AI-enabled products and services, including how vendors handle data, manage security and access, use information for model training, and respond to security incidents. Participants will learn what to look for when evaluating vendor practices and contractual protections and how to identify potential risks before committing to a tool.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Identify** key security and data protection questions to ask when evaluating AI-enabled products and vendors.
- **Assess** vendor practices related to data handling, access permissions, model training, and security incidents.
- **Recognize** potential risks and contractual protections to consider before adopting an AI-enabled tool or service.

## Speakers

- **Jae Yeon Kim**, Assistant Professor of Public Policy, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
- **James Saunders**, State Chief Information Security Officer, Maryland Department of Information Technology

## Moderators

- **Deborah Stine**, Senior Fellow, Innovate US

Part of the series [AI and Cybersecurity in the Public Sector for the Non-Expert](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/ai-and-cybersecurity-in-the-public-sector-for-the-non-expert).

# Scaling Government Innovation

InnovateUS workshop · 10 December 2026 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Many public agencies are experimenting with AI, but the harder work begins after a promising pilot. To create lasting public value, governments need ways to measure impact, sustain digital services, share what works, and build the internal capacity to keep improving over time.

In this workshop, you will explore how agencies can move from individual pilots to durable institutional capability. You will learn practical approaches for evaluating results, maintaining AI-enabled products, reusing solutions across agencies, and creating the culture and operating models needed to make innovation sustainable.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Measure **the impact of AI-enabled pilots using outcomes tied to service quality, efficiency, and public value.
- **Identify **practices for maintaining, adapting, and sharing reusable digital products across agencies.
- **Develop **strategies to build a sustainable culture of innovation and continuous improvement in government.

## Moderators

- **Anirudh Dinesh**, CTO, InnovateUS

Part of the series [AI Insourcing and the Government Product Model](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/ai-insourcing-and-the-government-product-model-).

Register on the workshop page: https://innovate-us.org/scaling-government-innovation

# What Works—and What Doesn't

InnovateUS workshop · 14 December 2026 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Agentic systems create new opportunities but also new risks. Drawing on lessons from early adopters, this session examines what agencies are learning about reliability, privacy and security, human oversight, transparency, accountability, and governance. Participants will leave with practical principles for deciding where agents are appropriate, where safeguards are required, and how to experiment, scale, and govern agentic systems responsibly.

InnovateUS workshop · 16 December 2026 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

This session explores how agencies can develop governance processes, escalation pathways, staff guidance, and cross-functional partnerships to support safer, more responsible AI adoption. Participants will learn how different roles across an organization can contribute to identifying, communicating, and managing AI-related risks.

# Workforce Planning, Job Design, and Skills-Based Hiring

InnovateUS workshop · 11 January 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Good hiring starts with a clear picture of how people can contribute and grow within the organization.   Understanding the skills and capability development that an agency needs now and in the future shapes everything from job classifications to job design to AI execution of routine tasks. This session explores how AI can help HR teams analyze staffing needs, identify skill gaps, and review outdated job classifications. It also looks at how AI can support skills-based hiring by clarifying core competencies and reconsidering unnecessary degree requirements. Participants will hear early lessons from a state-based project and discuss what it takes to open the door to a wider talent pool without lowering the bar on the achievement of critical outcomes.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Describe at least two ways AI can help analyze staffing needs, identify skill gaps, or flag outdated job classifications.

- Explain what skills-based hiring means in practice, including how clarifying core competencies can reduce reliance on unnecessary degree requirements.

- Name key takeaways from a public sector project that they could apply when starting a similar effort in their own agency.

Part of the series [AI for Public HR Professionals](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/ai-for-public-hr-professionals).

Register on the workshop page: https://innovate-us.org/using-ai-in-public-sector-hr-for-hr-professionals

# Preparing Communities for Infrastructure Development Conversations

InnovateUS workshop · 12 January 2027 · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Major infrastructure proposals can raise complex questions about jobs, public services, land use, environmental impacts, energy and water use, aesthetics, and other community priorities. Learn how state and local governments can help residents understand proposed developments and participate meaningfully in conversations and decisions that affect their communities.

Using data centers and other infrastructure projects as examples, explore practical approaches to sharing information, identifying affected communities, gathering local knowledge, surfacing priorities and concerns, and creating opportunities for dialogue before key decisions and commitments are made.

Part of the series [AI Data Centers: Community Engagement, Agreements, and Accountability](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/ai-data-centers-community-engagement-agreements-and-accountability).

Register on the workshop page: https://innovate-us.org/preparing-communities-for-infrastructure-development-conversations

# Asking Better Questions: Data Literacy 101

InnovateUS workshop · 14 January 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Good data analysis starts with understanding the question you are trying to answer. Learn how to turn everyday public sector challenges into questions that data can help address and identify what information you need to understand a problem, measure progress, or inform a decision.

Through hands-on exercises, explore different types of data, how datasets are structured, and how AI can help you explore data, formulate questions, and identify patterns worth investigating. At the same time, learn to assess whether the data you are working with is relevant, complete, representative, and appropriate to use, including considerations around sensitive information and privacy.

**Tool and opportunity:** Use data and AI to explore public sector questions and identify potential insights.
**Risk and responsibility:** Assess whether the underlying data is appropriate, reliable, representative, and safe to use.

Part of the series [Data Literacy for Public Service:Understanding and Using Data in the AI Age](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/data-literacy-for-public-service-understanding-and-using-data-in-the-ai-age).

Register on the workshop page: https://innovate-us.org/asking-better-questions-data-literacy-101

# Evaluating Accessibility at Scale: Using AI-Assisted Tools Responsibly

InnovateUS workshop · 14 January 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Conventional accessibility scanners can identify many common technical failures, but they detect only a portion of the barriers people encounter and may also generate false positives or other noise. AI-powered testing may extend automated detection by performing more complex interactions and interpreting contextual information. Examples include navigation menus that appear only on hover and autocomplete results that cannot be navigated by keyboard.

This session examines how AI-assisted evaluations work, what evidence is available about their performance, and how agencies can assess vendor claims about improved detection. Participants will hear perspectives from accessibility professionals and tool developers about efforts to automate portions of testing that have traditionally required people. The discussion will also consider reliability, bias, false results, and the continuing role of manual testing by accessibility professionals and assistive-technology users.

Part of the series [Using AI for Digital Accessibility](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/using-ai-for-digital-accessibility).

Register on the workshop page: https://innovate-us.org/evaluating-accessibility-at-scale-using-ai-assisted-tools-responsibly

# Recruiting, Onboarding, Learning, and Performance

InnovateUS workshop · 20 January 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Finding the right person for the right job depends on getting the word out, cultivating interest, making it easy to apply, identifying the right candidate, and then bringing them onboard and supporting their learning to achieve breakthrough performance. No area of the HR function is more exposed to workflow redesign through AI than these functions. The stakes for getting these core functions right could not be higher. An employee’s first weeks, and the chances they get to grow afterward, shape whether they stay in public service. This session looks at how AI has been deployed to create clearer, better outcomes at each stage of the process that links recruiting to outcomes, including how AI can make performance reviews more consistent, timely, and useful for both managers and employees. We will also look at AI mistakes and problems, including bias, failures of judgement, inflexibility, and privacy breaches. Join this session to learn how to achieve greater effectiveness and efficiency in core personnel development functions – and how to avoid the pitfalls.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Identify where AI is currently used across the recruiting-to-performance pipeline, from job postings and candidate screening to onboarding, learning support, and performance reviews.

- Describe how AI can support a fairer, more useful performance review process, and where human judgment must remain central.

- List practical questions to ask before adopting or expanding an AI tool for recruiting, onboarding, or performance management.

Part of the series [AI for Public HR Professionals](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/ai-for-public-hr-professionals).

# From Findings to Fixes: Improving Accessibility in Public Digital Services

AI-assisted tools increasingly offer suggested fixes or automated remediation for inaccessible websites and documents. These tools may work well for straightforward content, but their performance can vary considerably with forms, STEM materials, unconventional tables, and other complex content.

# Making Sense of Data: Statistics, Patterns, and Evidence

InnovateUS workshop · 21 January 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

You don't need to be a statistician to work effectively with data, but you do need to understand what the numbers can and cannot tell you. Learn how to interpret common statistics, percentages, rates, comparisons, charts, and trends using public sector examples.

Practice using AI to help analyze data, identify patterns, and create visualizations. Learn how to check the results and recognize common problems, including inappropriate comparisons, poor-quality or biased data, confusion between correlation and causation, misleading visualizations, and AI-generated analyses that appear convincing but are not supported by the evidence.

**Tool and opportunity:** Use AI to support analysis, identify patterns, and visualize data.
**Risk and responsibility:** Check the data, methods, and AI-assisted analysis before accepting the results or drawing conclusions.

Part of the series [Data Literacy for Public Service:Understanding and Using Data in the AI Age](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/data-literacy-for-public-service-understanding-and-using-data-in-the-ai-age).

# Pay, Benefits, and Workplace Wellbeing

InnovateUS workshop · 1 February 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Compensation and benefits administration involves high-volume, detail-heavy work where errors directly affect people’s lives. This session explores how AI could help HR teams spot pay inequities, reduce administrative burden, and help employees understand their benefits. It covers why decisions about individual pay and eligibility require judgement that demands humans in the loop.  Challenges include supporting employee wellbeing without crossing a line into surveillance; how to sustain compassion and human connection supported by AI; and how to understand well-being at a deeper and more substantial leve.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Describe how AI can help flag potential pay inequities and reduce administrative burden in compensation and benefits work.

- Distinguish between tasks AI can reasonably support and decisions about individual pay and eligibility that require a human in the loop.

- Recognize the line between using AI to support employee wellbeing and using it in ways that feel like surveillance.

Part of the series [AI for Public HR Professionals](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/ai-for-public-hr-professionals).

# HR Policy, Labor Partnership, and Workforce Transitions

InnovateUS workshop · 8 February 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

HR performance is defined by policies, partnerships, and the organization’s capability to make critical transitions toward new ways of doing things that reflect current priorities and values.  This session explores how agencies can develop HR policies for responsible AI use that are consistent with merit principles and civil service rules, and why unions and employees need to be partners in those decisions. It also looks at how AI can help agencies plan for succession and capture institutional knowledge when experienced employees retire or move on.  And it examines how AI enables talented employees to develop in ways that reflect shared goals.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Identify core elements of a responsible AI use policy for HR that aligns with merit principles and civil service rules.

- Explain why involving unions and employees early in AI decisions matters, and name at least one way to start that conversation.

- Describe how AI can support succession planning and help capture institutional knowledge before experienced employees leave.

# Building Support and Leading Your Team Through Change

InnovateUS workshop · 9 February 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Leading change requires building support in every direction: with the teams putting improvements into practice, the senior leaders who can help move them forward, and the colleagues whose work may be affected. Learn practical strategies for involving your team early, communicating why a change matters, and making a compelling case to decision-makers. Through real government examples, explore how to understand different perspectives, address concerns constructively, and build the trust, relationships, and shared commitment needed to turn plans into action.

## Learning goals

- Identify ways to involve their team early in shaping a change, so the people putting it into practice help design it.

- Explain why a change matters in terms that resonate with senior leaders, and outline a brief case for their support.

- Anticipate concerns from colleagues whose work may be affected, and plan a constructive way to address them.

# Skills: Turning Analysis into Decision-Relevant Information

InnovateUS workshop · 8 March 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Quantitative and qualitative analysis does not automatically answer the questions facing state and local governments. Staff must determine which questions to ask, assess the quality of available evidence, examine policy and program alternatives, and communicate tradeoffs.

This session explores how government practitioners use analytical skills to connect evidence with decisions and societal outcomes. Participants will examine how staff assess alternatives using the 4E's: effectiveness, efficiency, equity, and ease of political acceptability.

Speakers could draw on policies and programs involving energy planning, environmental protection, public health, infrastructure, emerging technologies, or economic development. # Stories: Connecting Analysis with Lived Experience

InnovateUS workshop · 10 March 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

Stories can show how people experience a policy, program, investment, or public problem. They can help government staff understand why an issue matters, who benefits, who encounters barriers, and how implementation differs from what aggregate measures suggest.

# Spaces: Localizing Evidence, Action, and Accountability

InnovateUS workshop · 12 March 2027 · 60 minutes · upcoming: registration on the workshop page

The same policy or program can produce different results across communities. Infrastructure and institutional capacity shape what can be implemented. Environmental and economic conditions influence the opportunities available, while public trust and previous government decisions affect how communities respond. Together, these conditions help determine who benefits and which challenges remain.

In this framework, spaces are more than meeting places. They include the geographic, institutional, workplace, professional, identity-based, and issue-based communities in which people live, work, organize, and experience the outcomes of government action.

This session examines how government staff connect skills and stories to these settings. Speakers will explore how policies and programs are adapted to local conditions, how governments recognize differences among communities, and how agencies determine whether their actions created meaningful opportunities or addressed important challenges.

Part of the series [From Evidence to Impact: Skills, Stories, and Spaces in State and Local Government](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/from-evidence-to-impact-skills-stories-and-spaces-in-state-and-local-government).

# Communicating Across Language and Cultural Barriers: Equity, Access, and Multilingual Outreach

InnovateUS workshop · 19 November 2026 · 60 minutes

A five-person comms team can now do things in twelve languages that used to require twelve contractors. That's the opportunity. The risk is doing it badly: machine-translated documents with no cultural context, sent into communities where trust was already thin. This session is the difference. We'll build a real multilingual workflow live, with AI doing the volume and humans doing the judgment, and cover the partnership strategies that make translated outreach land as intended rather than as an afterthought.

Participants will leave with:

- A framework for assessing whether their agency's communications are equitably reaching all constituents

- Practical plain-language and culturally responsive design principles that improve clarity for all audiences

- Strategies for building community partnerships that support authentic, trusted outreach to underserved populations

- A clear-eyed understanding of when and how to use AI translation and localization tools — and when human expertise must guide the work

## Speakers

- **Marelyn Rivera**, Founder & CEO, Conexión Strategies
- **Jess Moore Matthews**, Founder & Chief Good Troublemaker at Backbone Digital Leaders | Adjunct Faculty Member, New York University

## Moderators

- **Pearl Gabel**, Creative + Communications Consultant; former Digital Director, State of New Jersey; former Director of Video, City of New York

Part of the series [Amplify: Mastering Public Communication in the AI Age](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/mastering-public-communication-in-the-ai-age-series).

Recording: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L9GisbOqUeI

# Putting Public and Democratic AI into Practice

InnovateUS workshop · 18 November 2026 · 60 minutes

This closing session looks at concrete examples of how public institutions have used, built, or bought AI in ways that keep meaningful control in public hands. Participants will examine the choices that made these efforts work, what they required in money, skill, and political support, and the points where they ran into trouble or fell short. The emphasis is on how a given approach succeeded under particular conditions and what a public servant working under different constraints can reasonably take away. By the end, participants will be able to recognize where the openings for public and democratic AI exist in their own institutions and what it would take to act on them.

## Learning goals

- Understand how public institutions have harnessed AI in ways that preserve public control while delivering results.

- Recognize the conditions that allowed these efforts to work.

- Learn from where these efforts struggled or fell short.

- Identify realistic openings to apply public and democratic AI approaches in participants’ own work.

## Speakers

- **Magnus Sahlgren**, CEO, Hybridity and Senior Advisor, AI Sweden

## Moderators

- **Luca Cominassi**, Attorney-at-law, Public AI Fellow at MetaGov

Part of the series [Democratic and Public AI: Practical Strategies for Buying, Building, and Governing AI](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/public-ai-buying-and-building-for-civic-use).

Recording: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9SAGfBaNF3Q

# From Chatbots to Agents

InnovateUS workshop · 16 November 2026 · 60 minutes

AI agents are often described as the next generation of AI, but the reality is more nuanced. Most organizations move gradually from using AI for drafting and research to using AI that remembers context, automates tasks, coordinates workflows, and eventually takes action on a user's behalf. This session explores that evolution and explains how agents differ from chatbots, copilots, workflow automation, and traditional software tools. Drawing on early government examples, participants will learn where agencies are experimenting with agentic capabilities today and how to distinguish meaningful innovation from marketing hype.

## Speakers

- **Ray Bell**, AI/ML Product Director, State of Maryland
- **Deborah Stine**, Senior Fellow, Innovate US

Part of the series [Working with AI Agents in the Public Sector: What Works (and What Doesn’t)](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/working-with-ai-agents-in-the-public-sector-what-works-and-what-doesn-t).

# How Governments Are Buying AI Now

InnovateUS workshop · 16 November 2026 · 60 minutes

Governments and public bodies have many ways of acquiring AI tools: enterprise licenses, pilots, features embedded in software they already use, and heavily discounted offers built for the public sector. Each path solves some problems while carrying consequences for cost, flexibility, and the degree of control a government keeps over its own systems and data. This session maps how AI is entering public institutions today and what those acquisition choices set in motion. Participants will look at the patterns that shape this market, including deep discounting, centralized purchasing, closed ecosystems, and the unmanaged adoption of tools by staff, and consider how different options can either narrow or improve the future delivery of public services and government operations.

## Learning goals

- Understand the ways AI is currently acquired and used in government. 

- Recognize how common acquisition choices affect cost, flexibility, and control over data, models, and workflows.

- Identify where governments retain leverage to shape what they buy rather than accept default terms.

- Assess how a current or recent AI acquisition in their own context is likely to shape their options going forward.

## Speakers

- **Leonardo Quattrucci**, Chief Growth Officer, Arq Foundation
- **Karolis Granickas**, Head of Europe and Central Asia, Open Contracting Partnership (OCP)

## Moderators

- **Luca Cominassi**, Attorney-at-law, Public AI Fellow at MetaGov

Part of the series [Democratic and Public AI: Practical Strategies for Buying, Building, and Governing AI](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/public-ai-buying-and-building-for-civic-use).

# Explaining AI: How Communicators Can Explain What Their Agency Is Doing with AI

InnovateUS workshop · 12 November 2026 · 60 minutes

Your agency is probably already using AI to process applications, flag fraud, or route services. Most residents don't know. When they find out, they'll have three questions: Who's accountable? Can it be wrong? What happens to my data? The communicators who can answer plainly will build trust. The ones who reach for jargon or evasion will spend years rebuilding it. What does the public actually want to know about government AI, how to explain algorithmic decisions without a computer science degree on either end, and what to say when the system gets it wrong. Because it will, and your answer for that day should already exist.

Participants will leave with:

- A working understanding of how government AI systems operate and where they are most commonly deployed

- Frameworks for explaining algorithmic decision-making to non-technical audiences in plain, credible language

- Strategies for communicating accountability, oversight, and human review in AI-assisted processes

- Practical messaging approaches for common scenarios, including service delivery, benefits, and law enforcement applications

- **Lee Rainie**, Director, Imagining the Digital Future Center, Elon University

# Building AI With Your Workforce: Workers as Co-Designers

InnovateUS workshop · 10 November 2026 · 60 minutes

Even with trust and governance in place, many agencies still design and deploy AI tools without ever bringing frontline workers into the actual development process. This closing workshop explores what it looks like to go a step further: treating workers not just as stakeholders to consult, but as co-designers with real influence over how tools are built and implemented. Speakers will share frameworks and examples for involving frontline staff throughout the design and rollout process, so that the resulting tools reflect the realities of the job and the judgment of the people doing it.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Understand the difference between consulting workers and genuinely co-designing AI tools with them.

- Identify practical methods for involving frontline staff in the design, testing, and rollout of new AI tools.

- Apply co-design principles to their own agency's AI implementation process, from pilot through full deployment.

# From Projects to Products

InnovateUS workshop · 9 November 2026 · 60 minutes

Too often, government technology work is organized around one-time projects: launch a system, close the contract, and move on. But residents’ needs, policy requirements, and service conditions continue to change after launch.

In this workshop, you will explore how public agencies can shift toward a product mindset focused on continuous improvement, user needs, and measurable public outcomes. You will learn what product management looks like in government and how teams can use feedback, data, and iteration to build services that keep improving over time.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Distinguish **between project-based and product-based approaches to government technology.
- **Apply** a product mindset centered on user needs, continuous improvement, and public outcomes.
- **Identify **practices teams can use to prioritize, measure, and improve digital services over time.

# What is Public and Democratic AI and Why it Matters

InnovateUS workshop · 9 November 2026 · 60 minutes

A growing set of efforts argues that the public should have a more direct stake in how AI systems are built and overseen. This idea travels under several names, public AI and democratic AI among them. At its core, this idea calls for greater public involvement in AI, more transparency and accountability in how those systems operate, and infrastructure that is open and shared rather than controlled by a single vendor. This session works through what these features mean on a practical level and why proponents believe they produce systems that are both more accountable and more capable. The goal is to give participants a clear and critical understanding of what public and democratic AI offers, what it asks of the government, and why the distinction from a purely commercial approach matters for their work.

## Learning goals

- Understand what public and democratic AI means in practice.

- Understand the arguments for and against a greater public role in AI.

- Connect these ideas to the concrete decisions about building, buying, governing, and using AI that participants face in their own work.

## Speakers

- **Alek Tarkowski**, Director of Strategy, Open Future
- **Joshua Tan**, CTO, Current AI & Public AI

## Moderators

- **Luca Cominassi**, Attorney-at-law, Public AI Fellow at MetaGov

Part of the series [Democratic and Public AI: Practical Strategies for Buying, Building, and Governing AI](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/public-ai-buying-and-building-for-civic-use).

# Communicating in a Fragmented Media Landscape: Reaching Audiences Across Platforms and Echo Chambers

InnovateUS workshop · 5 November 2026 · 60 minutes

A press release, a press conference, the local paper, a public meeting. That used to be the whole job. Now your residents are split across newsletters, podcasts, group chats, and short-form video, sorted by algorithms into audiences that never overlap, and a growing number ask ChatGPT about government services instead of visiting your website. What the AI says about your agency is your communication, whether you wrote it or not. This session covers how to show up across a fractured landscape without fracturing your message: adapting to each platform while sounding like one credible voice, reaching low-trust and ideologically distinct communities, and getting your content found when the searcher is a language model.

Participants will leave with:

- A clearer picture of today's fragmented media landscape and what it means for public sector outreach

- Practical frameworks for adapting messages across platforms while maintaining a consistent, trustworthy voice

- Strategies for reaching audiences in echo chambers and low-trust information environments

- Tools for using audience data and platform analytics to inform — not replace — human communication decisions

## Speakers

- **Michael Appleton**, Photographer, Office of the Mayor of New York City

## Moderators

- **Pearl Gabel**, Creative + Communications Consultant; former Digital Director, State of New Jersey; former Director of Video, City of New York

Part of the series [Amplify: Mastering Public Communication in the AI Age](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/mastering-public-communication-in-the-ai-age-series).

# AI Changes: Buy vs. Build

InnovateUS workshop · 4 November 2026 · 60 minutes

AI is changing the choices public agencies face when planning new technology. Work that once required lengthy procurements or expensive custom software can now sometimes be prototyped, tested, or improved by public-sector teams using generative and agentic AI.

In this workshop, you will explore how AI is changing the economics of government technology and what that means for buy-versus-build decisions. You will learn how to assess when to purchase commercial tools, when to build internally, and when to combine both approaches to create services that are sustainable, accountable, and valuable to the public.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Assess **how generative and agentic AI are changing buy-versus-build decisions in government.
- **Identify **when to buy, build, or combine commercial and internally developed solutions.
- **Evaluate **tradeoffs around cost, speed, sustainability, accountability, and public value.

- **Michael Boyce**, Senior AI Advisor, State of Maryland
- **Jeffery Marino**, Director, Office of Data and Innovation, State of California

# Governance With Workers: Building Joint Frameworks

InnovateUS workshop · 2 November 2026 · 60 minutes

Trust-building conversations are a starting point — but lasting change requires structure. This workshop looks at how public agencies and their unions have moved beyond one-off conversations to build joint governance frameworks that give workers a real, ongoing role in shaping AI policy. Drawing on real examples, speakers will discuss what it takes to design governance structures, including policies, standards, and guardrails, where power over AI decisions is genuinely shared between management and labor.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Understand what joint governance structures for workplace AI can look like in practice.

- Identify the legal and contractual mechanisms unions and agencies have used to formalize worker input on AI policy.

- Apply lessons from cities that have negotiated worker protections into their AI policies to their own agency's governance planning.

# The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly

InnovateUS workshop · 27 October 2026 · 60 minutes

Some predictive systems have helped governments improve inspections, anticipate service needs, target interventions, and allocate resources more effectively. Others have failed because of poor data, flawed assumptions, feedback loops, bias, or misplaced confidence in uncertain forecasts. Through real-world examples, participants will examine both successful and unsuccessful deployments of predictive AI and learn how to identify common warning signs, limitations, and unintended consequences before they become costly mistakes.

## Speakers

- **Aleksandra Korolova**, Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Public Affairs, Princeton University

## Moderators

- **Mihir Kshirsagar**, Tech Policy Clinic Lead, Princeton University

Part of the series [The Good, the Bad and the Ugly of Predictive AI](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/the-good-the-bad-and-the-ugly-of-predictive-ai).

# Talking to Your Workers: Trust Before Technology

InnovateUS workshop · 26 October 2026 · 60 minutes

Before an agency chooses a tool, vendor, or rollout timeline, it needs to have an honest conversation with the people who will actually use the technology. This opening workshop focuses on how public sector managers can approach those conversations — not as a one-time announcement, but as an ongoing dialogue that builds trust rather than anxiety. Speakers from government and organized labor will share what it looks like to talk openly with workers about what AI adoption means for their jobs, their expertise, and their rights, and why starting with trust — rather than a finished plan — leads to better outcomes for everyone involved.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Recognize why early, honest communication with workers changes the trajectory of AI adoption.

- Identify common sources of worker anxiety around AI and practical ways managers can address them directly.

- Describe approaches for talking transparently about job impact, worker expertise, and legal rights before technology decisions are finalized.

- **Jim Brown**, Former Division Chief, Monterey Fire Department

# Benefits Access and Delivery: Using AI to Expand Reach, Simply Systems, and Improve Integrity

InnovateUS workshop · 22 October 2026 · 60 minutes

Public health outcomes are shaped not only by healthcare, but also by whether residents can successfully access the benefits and supports available to them. Yet public benefits systems remain difficult to navigate, fragmented across agencies, and burdensome for both residents and administrators. This session explores how artificial intelligence can help modernize access while preserving equity, privacy, and public trust.

Participants will examine how AI tools can simplify enrollment and improve service delivery through intelligent assistants, user-centered application experiences, and emerging agentic approaches that support form completion and guide users through complex processes. The session will also explore how AI can help connect traditionally separate systems—aligning health, nutrition, housing, and income supports while identifying eligibility across multiple programs.

And, the workshop will examine how AI can strengthen program integrity and administrative effectiveness through better data coordination, fraud detection, and improved decision support. Throughout, participants will learn more about governance, consent, and implementation questions that agencies must address to ensure these tools expand access rather than create new barriers.

# Health Information in the AI Era: Combating Misinformation and Reaching the Public

InnovateUS workshop · 15 October 2026 · 60 minutes

Public health agencies are entering a new information environment in which artificial intelligence is changing not only how information is created and distributed, but also how residents search for, interpret, and trust health guidance. AI has the potential to accelerate misinformation and deepen confusion—but it also creates new opportunities for public institutions to communicate more effectively and build stronger relationships with communities.

This session explores the evolving landscape of health misinformation and examines how AI can both amplify and counter these dynamics. Participants will discuss approaches for evaluating and monitoring AI-enabled communication systems and consider how public agencies can use these tools responsibly.

The workshop will focus on practical strategies already beginning to emerge across the field, including AI-powered chatbots that provide trusted guidance, community-based information channels and kiosks, and more personalized communication approaches. The goal is to help participants move beyond passive information delivery toward more responsive, adaptive, and trusted forms of public engagement.

# The Basics and the Breakthrough Opportunities

InnovateUS workshop · 8 October 2026 · 60 minutes

Public health is one of the most important—and underdeveloped—frontiers for artificial intelligence. While AI is rapidly reshaping clinical care, its application in public health remains early, fragmented, and full of untapped potential. This session introduces participants to the current state of the field and provides a practical foundation for understanding how AI can support population health goals.

Participants will receive a clear, accessible introduction to core AI concepts and explore how they connect to established public health methods including epidemiology and real-world evidence. The session will examine approaches for developing ethical and responsible AI systems that center human and community agency and discuss how public health leaders can begin building AI literacy and readiness within their organizations.

The workshop will also address why adoption has moved slowly despite growing interest. Participants will explore common barriers—including fragmented data systems, weak cross-agency coordination, institutional risk aversion, and complex governance environments—and leave with a practical understanding of why advancing an AI-enabled public health agenda has become increasingly urgent for improving outcomes and reducing harms such as misinformation and inequitable access.

# Try Before and After You Buy

InnovateUS workshop · 29 September 2026 · 60 minutes

How can agencies assess whether an AI tool is likely to work before committing significant resources? This session covers practical methods for testing AI systems prior to procurement or deployment, including baseline comparisons, pilot design, task-based evaluation, and the identification of acceptable and unacceptable risks. Also, performance can change as models evolve, workflows shift, staff adapt their practices, and systems encounter new contexts and use cases. This session explores how agencies can monitor performance over time, detect emerging problems, and understand when an initially successful implementation may require adjustment or reevaluation.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Design** practical pre-deployment evaluations that compare AI performance against current practices and establish meaningful baselines.
- **Identify** acceptable and unacceptable risks through task-based testing and well-designed pilots before committing significant resources to AI adoption.
- **Develop** approaches for monitoring AI performance over time and determining when changes in models, workflows, or use cases require adjustment, reevaluation, or retirement.

## Speakers

- **Patrick McLoughlin**, Executive Director, Maryland Benefits, State of Maryland; Former MD State Chief Data Officer
- **Kathrin Frauscher**, Deputy Executive Director, Open Contracting Partnership

## Moderators

- **Deborah Stine**, Senior Fellow, Innovate US

# Getting Started Without Getting Overwhelmed - How procurement teams are taking their first AI steps

InnovateUS workshop · 28 September 2026 · 60 minutes

Learn how procurement teams are taking their first steps with AI without a big budget or a dedicated tech team. Two practitioner stories show how a "start small" approach can turn a routine, time-consuming task into a quick, reliable one, and how a small, resourceful team found its own starting point without extra resources. Walk away with a practical way to identify where AI can support your team's work first.

## Learning goals

- Identify a small, low-risk task in your own procurement process where AI could save time or reduce error

- Recognize what conditions (data, tools, staff buy-in) make a first AI project more likely to succeed

- Apply a simple framework for scoping and piloting a first AI use case in your organization

# Policy Choices, Investment Strategies, and Governance

InnovateUS workshop · 24 September 2026 · 60 minutes

Governments face difficult choices as AI-related infrastructure expands and AI becomes more integrated into energy and environmental systems. This session examines policy, regulatory, planning, procurement, and investment approaches being used to manage growth, protect communities, support innovation, maintain grid reliability, and advance environmental goals. Participants will explore the tradeoffs associated with different approaches and the questions public officials should ask before making decisions.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Compare** policy, regulatory, procurement, planning, and investment approaches for managing AI-related infrastructure and applications.
- **Analyze** tradeoffs among economic development, community impacts, grid reliability, innovation, affordability, and environmental goals.
- **Identify** key questions public officials should ask when making decisions about AI-related infrastructure, investments, and governance.

# Comparing Humans, AI, and Human-AI Teams

InnovateUS workshop · 22 September 2026 · 60 minutes

The most important question is often not whether AI performs well in isolation, but whether it improves performance relative to current practice. This session explores methods for comparing human-only, AI-only, and human-plus-AI workflows and identifying where AI adds value, where it creates risks, and where hybrid approaches perform best.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Compare** the performance of human-only, AI-only, and human-plus-AI approaches across real-world government tasks and workflows.
- **Identify** where AI can improve current practices, where it may introduce new risks, and where human judgment and oversight remain essential.
- **Evaluate** when hybrid human-AI approaches can deliver better performance, reliability, and public outcomes than either humans or AI working alone.

- **Vera Liao**, Associate Professor, University of Michigan
- **Amy Perez**, Nonresident Policy Fellow at Stanford's Regulation, Evaluation, and Governance Lab (RegLab)

# Measuring What Matters

InnovateUS workshop · 15 September 2026 · 60 minutes

Many AI evaluations focus on efficiency metrics such as time saved, documents processed, or staff hours reduced. This session examines how agencies can move beyond productivity measures to define success in terms of service quality, accuracy, equity, public trust, resident and worker experience, and public outcomes. Participants will learn practical approaches for identifying meaningful measures of public value.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Distinguish** between efficiency metrics and broader measures of AI effectiveness and public value.
- **Identify** meaningful measures of success across service quality, accuracy, equity, public trust, and resident and worker experience.
- **Develop** practical measures for evaluating whether AI use is improving public services and contributing to better outcomes.

# Why Measuring AI Is Hard

InnovateUS workshop · 8 September 2026 · 60 minutes

AI systems routinely achieve impressive scores on standardized tests and benchmarks, yet those results often tell us little about whether a tool will succeed in a real government setting.
This session explores the limitations of common AI benchmarks, the differences between predictive and generative AI systems, and why performance in laboratory tests often fails to predict success in real-world settings.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- **Explain** why standard AI benchmarks and test scores may not predict how well an AI system will perform on real government tasks and workflows.
- **Distinguish** key evaluation challenges for predictive and generative AI systems and identify why each requires different approaches to measuring performance.
- **Identify** the factors agencies should consider when defining meaningful measures of AI effectiveness, reliability, and public value in real-world government settings.

## Speakers

- **Arvind Narayanan**, Professor at Princeton University & Director of the Center for Information Technology Policy

## Moderators

# Helping the Helpers: AI Tools for Frontline Resident Service

InnovateUS workshop · 15 July 2026 · 60 minutes

This workshop explores how governments are using AI to help frontline staff answer resident questions more accurately, navigate complex policies more efficiently, and provide better service across public contact centers. Rather than replacing workers, these tools are designed to help staff find information faster, reduce time spent searching across systems, and handle a wider range of resident inquiries with confidence. Drawing on examples, including the MassHealth Helper initiative in Massachusetts, participants will examine emerging approaches to AI-assisted resident service, lessons from implementation, and practical considerations for deploying these tools responsibly.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Understand how tools like MassHealth Helper can support contact center staff in delivering faster, more accurate service to residents. 

- Evaluate the opportunities and limitations of retrieval-augmented generation and similar tools in high-stakes public service contexts.

- Identify key considerations for implementing new tools in contact centers responsibly, including trust, equity, and maintaining human support.

## Speakers

- **Beji Joseph**, Deputy Director, MassHealth Medicaid Systems Development
- **Tosin Adebiyi**, Director - Special Eligibility Programs and Audits (SEPA) MassHealth

# Inside the Modernization of High-Volume Call Centers

InnovateUS workshop · 8 July 2026 · 60 minutes

Public benefits programs field enormous call volumes — and the pressure on those systems became impossible to ignore during and after the pandemic. This workshop features practitioners from two state agencies who led call center modernization efforts from the inside. Speakers will share what the modernization process actually looks like — what prompted the effort, what they changed, what was harder than expected, and how it is impacting the lives of everyday residents. Participants will come away with a grounded, practitioner perspective on what it takes to redesign high-stakes, high-volume contact center operations within the real constraints of a public agency.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Describe the drivers and process behind real call center modernization efforts in state government. 

- Identify common operational and organizational challenges agencies face when redesigning phone-based services. 

- Apply lessons from a public benefits context to diagnose improvement opportunities in their own agencies.

# What Responsive Government Looks Like: Designing Effective Public Contact Centers

InnovateUS workshop · 1 July 2026 · 60 minutes

Public contact centers are often the primary way residents interact with government,  yet many were built for a different era and haven't kept pace with resident expectations or modern service delivery. This workshop brings together practitioners who work alongside government agencies to modernize how public services are designed and delivered.

Drawing on their experience, the speakers will share what they've learned about what makes contact center modernization succeed or stall, where the biggest opportunities for improvement tend to lie, and how to build the case for change from the inside. Participants will learn about real examples leave with a clearer picture of what resident-centered contact center operations can look like — and a practical lens for evaluating their own.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to

- - Identify the core components of an effective, resident-centered public contact center.

  - Recognize common barriers to modernization and where contact center systems most often break down.

  - Describe strategies that innovation teams use to help agencies improve access, consistency, and responsiveness in resident interactions.

# The Prompting Lab Office Hours: Bring Your AI Questions

InnovateUS workshop · 26 June 2026 · 30 minutes

After learning the basics of prompt structure, the next step is practice. This follow-up office hours session gives you a chance to bring your questions, test prompts, troubleshoot challenges, and learn from peers who are also beginning to use generative AI in their work.
Led as an interactive, peer-to-peer session, this office hours workshop will help you refine prompts for real public sector tasks, from drafting emails and summarizing documents to preparing meeting materials, translating complex ideas into plain language, or organizing information. You will have space to ask what is working, what is not, and how to improve your prompts while keeping accuracy, judgment, privacy, and accountability in mind.
This session is designed for public professionals who attended the introductory Prompting Lab or who already understand the basic elements of a prompt and want guided practice

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Improve prompts based on feedback, examples, and peer discussion.
- Troubleshoot common prompting challenges, including unclear outputs, wrong tone, missing context, or overly broad responses.
- Adapt prompt structures to fit different public sector tasks and audiences.
- Assess when an AI-generated response needs revision, verification, or additional human judgment.
- Share practical prompting approaches that can be applied in day-to-day government work.

- **Stephan Schmidt**, AI Producer, The Burnes Center for Social Change

# Invisible Barriers: Disability Rights and Public Sector AI

InnovateUS workshop · 25 June 2026 · 60 minutes

As governments adopt artificial intelligence to improve efficiency and service delivery, disability rights and accessibility are increasingly becoming central governance concerns rather than niche technical issues. Yet many AI systems are still built on datasets, assumptions, and design practices that fail to account for the diverse ways people interact with technology, including through screen readers, voice navigation, captioning, alternative input devices, and other assistive technologies. These invisible barriers can unintentionally exclude people with disabilities from public services, employment opportunities, education systems, healthcare access, and civic participation.

This workshop moves beyond high-level discussions of responsible AI to focus on practical public-sector challenges and decisions. Participants will examine how AI-enabled systems can either improve or undermine accessibility depending on how they are designed, procured, implemented, and monitored. Drawing on emerging public-sector guidance, accessibility initiatives, and disability-rights research, the session explores practical strategies agencies can use to build more accessible, equitable, and trustworthy AI-enabled services.

## Learning goals

- Provide an overview of the challenges and opportunities that people with disabilities face when using generative AI at the desktop level and its applications in state and local governments

- Identify organizational and operational challenges governments face, including workforce capacity, procurement constraints, vendor oversight, legacy systems, accessibility testing, DOJ Title II digital accessibility requirements and WCAG standards

- Explore practical ways AI may strengthen accessibility, such as improving compatibility with screen readers, supporting document remediation, generating captions and alt text, enhancing navigation, and assisting communication now and in the future

## Speakers

- **Ariana Aboulafia**, Disability Rights Advocate and Project Lead, Center for Democracy & Technology
- **Jay Wyant**, Chief Information Accessibility Officer (CIAO), State of Minnesota
- **Aaron Page**, Vice President Accessibility, Allyant
- **Marie Cohan**, Statewide Digital Accessibility Officer, Texas Department of Information Resources

## Moderators

- **Deborah Stine**, Senior Fellow, Innovate US

Part of the series [Elephants in the AI Room](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/elephants-in-the-ai-room).

# Power, Place, and AI: Energy, Environment, and AI Data Centers

InnovateUS workshop · 23 June 2026 · 60 minutes

As artificial intelligence expands across government, business, and everyday life, state and local leaders are increasingly confronting the physical infrastructure required to support it. AI systems rely on energy-intensive data centers, large amounts of electricity and water, extensive cooling systems, and expanded transmission and digital infrastructure. These developments can create opportunities for economic growth, workforce development, and grid modernization, but they also raise concerns about energy affordability, environmental impacts, land use, and noise pollution in both urban and rural communities.

AI may, however, also help governments improve energy efficiency, infrastructure planning, environmental monitoring, and public service delivery. This session examines the practical policy and governance challenges surrounding AI infrastructure and explores how public leaders can balance innovation, reliability, sustainability, affordability, and community impacts as AI adoption accelerates.

## Learning goals

- Understand how AI infrastructure affects energy systems, communities, and local environments

- Examine issues such as job creation, electricity demand, affordability, water use, and noise pollution

- Explore differences in how AI infrastructure may impact urban and rural communities

- Identify potential opportunities for AI to support energy efficiency and public-sector planning

- Consider practical governance and policy challenges facing state and local governments

## Speakers

- **Jessica Shirley**, Secretary, Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection
- **Michael Jung**, Co-Chair, Oregon Data Center Advisory Committee
- **Laura Jay**, Deputy Director, Climate Mayors

# Prompting Lab: The Elements of a Good Prompt

InnovateUS workshop · 12 June 2026 · 60 minutes

Getting useful results from generative AI starts with knowing how to ask the right question. For public professionals who are new to AI tools, prompting can feel like guesswork: What information should you include? How much context is enough? How do you ask for the tone, format, or level of detail you need?

In this beginner-friendly Prompting Lab, you will learn the basic structure of an effective prompt and practice building prompts that support everyday public sector work. We will break down key elements such as context, task, role, audience, tone, format, examples, and constraints. Through practical exercises, you will learn how to move from a vague request to a clearer, more useful prompt that keeps human judgment, accuracy, and accountability at the center.

This workshop is designed for public professionals who are starting to use generative AI and want a practical, low-pressure introduction to prompting.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Identify the core elements of a strong prompt, including context, task, role, tone, audience, format, and constraints.
- Apply a simple prompt structure to common public sector tasks such as drafting, summarizing, planning, and simplifying information.
- Revise vague prompts to make them clearer, more specific, and better aligned with the intended outcome.
- Evaluate AI-generated responses for usefulness, accuracy, tone, and fit for public sector work.
- Use prompting practices that support transparency, human oversight, and responsible use of AI.

## Speakers

- **Stephan Schmidt**, AI Producer, The Burnes Center for Social Change

# Beyond Displacement: Building an AI-Ready Workforce

InnovateUS workshop · 11 June 2026 · 60 minutes

AI is already changing how public employees draft emails and documents, analyze, communicate, and deliver services. For governments, the workforce question is not only whether AI will replace jobs, but how agencies can shape adoption so that workers are heard, and receive appropriate training so they are able to focus more on the mission that brought them to public service in the first place, rather than looking over forms, copying and pasting from spreadsheets, and data entry.

This session explores the workforce impacts of AI in the public sector, including displacement risks, changing roles, productivity pressures, and opportunities to make public work more enjoyable, effective and sustainable. Participants will examine strategies for workforce planning, worker engagement, training, and policy design that help agencies prepare for AI while protecting dignity, accountability, and service quality.

This workshop is designed for public professionals involved in workforce planning, operations, labor relations, service delivery, AI adoption, human resources, and organizational change.

## Learning goals

By the end of this session, participants will be able to:

- Describe how AI and automation may affect public sector roles, tasks, and working conditions.

- Identify opportunities for AI to improve public work while recognizing risks related to displacement, deskilling, surveillance, and productivity pressure.

- Apply strategies for engaging workers in AI adoption, including consultation, training, feedback loops, and shared governance.

- Evaluate policy and management tools that can help agencies strengthen worker power, build AI-ready skills, and protect public service quality.

## Speakers

- **Rob Asaro Angelo**, Senior Fellow, Burnes Center for Social Change & Professor, Northeastern University
- **Vanitha Zacharias**, Chief AI Strategist and Head of Technology Governance, Department of Administrative Services, State of Ohio

# Enabling great performance

InnovateUS workshop · 22 May 2026 · 60 minutes

Organizations take on lives of their own.  They have cultures, routines, and obligations.  They become known for doing things in certain ways.   Over time, these qualities of an organization may lose their relevance.   How can an organization be designed and redesigned for great performance?  

In this session, we will look at the challenge of adapting organizations over time in ways that both preserve core values and reflect what’s currently important.   Most public organizations are designed to fulfill mandates with equanimity, transparency, and accountability.   Because resources are scarce, efficiency becomes paramount.   We will look at how you can innovate despite all the obstacles that come with responsibility and scale.   You will leave inspired and strengthened for taking on critical challenges in ways that you may not have previously considered.

## Learning goals

Participants will:

- Understand the organizational features, such as culture, routines, and legacy structures, that can support performance or make adaptation more difficult over time.

- Explore how public organizations can balance innovation with core responsibilities such as accountability, transparency, equity, and efficiency.

- Identify practical approaches for redesigning organizations in ways that respond to new challenges while strengthening long-term effectiveness and mission alignment.

# Crafting AI Use Policies

InnovateUS workshop · 20 May 2026 · 60 minutes

This session provides guidance on developing robust policies for AI usage within a government setting. The session provides a framework for structuring a comprehensive AI use policy, including security, privacy, transparency, equity, accountability and oversight, and effectiveness. Through case studies and policy examples, attendees will learn how to draft comprehensive AI use policies that protect clients, increase efficiency, and maintain public trust.

## Learning goals

1. Draft a comprehensive AI use policy that addresses security, privacy, and equity considerations specific to a government setting.

 2. Apply real-world case studies and policy examples to identify best practices and common pitfalls when implementing AI governance frameworks.

 3. Balance operational efficiency with public accountability by building oversight and transparency mechanisms into AI use policies.

## Speakers

- **Marlene Biener**, Chief Operating Officer, Association of Prosecuting Attorneys

# Giving and receiving feedback

InnovateUS workshop · 18 May 2026 · 60 minutes

Most of us do not like getting formal performance feedback.   Most of us also do not like giving it.  There are many reasons why, including especially the amplification of the organization’s needs above those of each of us as individuals, and the difficulty of communicating effectively.    

How can a dreaded feedback meeting be turned into a good experience?   We’ll begin by looking at the needs of the person receiving the feedback.  What kinds of information are truly useful?  What are the barriers for the person under evaluation that make a feedback meeting hard to take?    We will then turn to the person who gives the feedback.  How can someone who is in this spot create an environment in which the individual truly benefits from worthwhile insights?

We will draw on recent research that suggests some answers to these questions.  This research also offers insights on ways that an individual can benefit more than customarily occurs.

## Learning goals

Participants will:

- Understand the common barriers that make performance feedback difficult to give, receive, and use effectively.

- Identify what kinds of feedback are most helpful to recipients and how to create conditions that make feedback easier to hear and act on.

- Learn practical strategies for delivering and engaging with feedback in ways that support growth, clearer communication, and stronger performance.

## Speakers

- **Anita McGahan**, Senior Research Scientist, The Burnes Center for Social Change

Part of the series [Foundations of Leadership: Leading Teams, Change, and Public Impact](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/leading-teams-change-and-public-impact).

Recording: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ld3sCjMYvKo

The transcript of the recording is in this workshop's Markdown copy: https://innovate-us.org/giving-and-receiving-feedback.md

# Understanding personal strengths

InnovateUS workshop · 15 May 2026 · 60 minutes

Most of us spend a great deal of time trying to overcome our weaknesses.  Indeed, performance feedback tends to center on gaps between our individual behavior and the optimum for the organization.   We are hardwired to focus on our deficiencies.  As much effort and time that we spend on trying to be better at things that an organization needs but that are not in our sweet spots, the hard truth is that our best contributors are not likely to be built on achieving this alignment.  It is our strengths that lead us to greatness.   

In this session, you will have a chance to take stock of what you do when you’re at your very best.   We will think about what your best collaborators would say about you.   What do you love to do?   And what will it take to do more of what makes you great?   In your organization, what enables you to focus?  And what dumps you into the morass of striving to overcome your weaknesses?  We will end with some tools that you can use to make a plan for your personal development that draws on these insights.

## Learning goals

Participants will:

- Identify the strengths, habits, and contributions that are most closely associated with their best work.

- Reflect on the organizational conditions, relationships, and responsibilities that support or hinder their ability to contribute at a high level.

- Develop a practical approach to personal development that builds on strengths while making more intentional choices about growth, focus, and impact.

## Speakers

- **Anita McGahan**, Senior Research Scientist, The Burnes Center for Social Change

Part of the series [Foundations of Leadership: Leading Teams, Change, and Public Impact](https://innovate-us.org/workshop-series/leading-teams-change-and-public-impact).

# Ten Things To Know About Data Centers

InnovateUS workshop · 14 May 2026 · 60 minutes

As governments explore and adopt AI, the conversation often centers on tools and use cases—but rarely on the infrastructure that makes it all possible. Data centers, the physical backbone of AI, are rapidly expanding, bringing new pressures on energy systems, land use, water resources, and community relations. For public professionals, these are no longer abstract technical issues—they are policy, planning, and governance challenges.

In this session, you will build a practical understanding of how data centers work and what drives their growth. You will examine how decisions about siting, energy consumption, resilience, and community impact intersect with public priorities.

## Learning goals

By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

- Explain the core components of data centers and how they support AI systems

- Assess the policy and planning implications of data center growth, including energy and land use

- Evaluate tradeoffs related to sustainability, resilience, and community impact

- Identify key questions to ask when reviewing or approving data center projects

- Apply practical considerations to align data center development with public goals and constraints
